X.note: This is a drone view over a low-detail block model. The roofs are huge, flat grey slabs, and the terracotta pyramids carry a repeating noise texture. Façades are tiny, uniform window grids with almost no weathering, shopfronts or signage. The street is a dark, empty strip. It reads as an early massing model, not Main Street. Nothing swims across the four frames. The camera only moves a little.

Y.note: This is practically the same render as X. Façades look slightly cooler and cleaner, and the street is just as empty and dark. It has the same toy-like massing, flat roofs and thin detail, and the textures stay locked across frames. I can't see a meaningful improvement over X.

why: The two are almost identical, both toy-like block models with flat roofs and sparse façade detail, and Y's façades are only marginally cleaner.
anachronisms_seen: flat concrete-style roofs with no period rooftop clutter or water tanks
no vehicles, signage or people to anchor 1943
